decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I need to pick three Pokémon against their Garchomp, Rotom-Wash, Scizor, Incineroar, Gholdengo, and Ninetales-Alola. Incineroar looks like a strong lead with Intimidate, Fake Out, and Parting Shot, while Gholdengo could threaten Rotom-Wash with its special attacks, and I'm weighing Garchomp's matchup against their lineup too.

I'm checking type matchups carefully: Scizor resists Dark but Kingambit's Iron Head is still fine against it, and I'm worried Ninetales-Alola's Ice Beam threatens my Garchomp if I bring it, though Archaludon's Steel/Dragon typing isn't weak to Ice so that's a safer option. I'm leaning toward Incineroar, Gholdengo, and a third pick, still working through whether Gholdengo's Shadow Ball actually beats Rotom-Wash given its Electric/Water typing.

Settling on Incineroar, Garchomp, and Gholdengo as my team — Garchomp's Earthquake hits Scizor super effectively and their Incineroar isn't weak to Ground, so this trio covers the key threats well.

decisions.hidden_reasoning: Since Garchomp outspeeds my Incineroar, Fake Out is the ideal opener—it flinches them out of using Outrage or Earthquake this turn while chipping some damage. I'll go with Fake Out.

decisions.thought: 98% MOVE: earthquake, 1% MOVE: stoneedge, 1% SWITCH: rotomwash

Flare Blitz is resisted by Dragon and gives recoil, plus Rough Skin punishes contact. Parting Shot drops the opposing Garchomp's Attack again and pivots Incineroar out for Gholdengo, a special attacker that Garchomp's physical attacks don't threaten much.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm weighing attack options against the weakened Garchomp, considering Flare Blitz's effectiveness given Fire's resistance to Dragon-types.

Parting Shot seems smarter—it cripples Garchomp's stats while letting me switch, and Gholdengo looks like a solid pivot since Steel/Ghost typing handles Garchomp reasonably well and its special attacks like Make It Rain stay strong regardless of the physical drop.

Actually Gholdengo switching in against their Garchomp works better since it's special-based and resists the physical Outrage/EQ threat, while Parting Shot would just drop Garchomp's attack further before the swap.

Outrage is super effective here, since Dragon hits their Dragon/Ground Garchomp for 2x with STAB. Their Attack is at -2, so their counterplay is weak, and our Garchomp should KO their 85% HP Garchomp before it can threaten us much.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Comparing speed and stat drops between the two Garchomps—ours is faster and the opponent's attack is lowered by two stages plus a special attack drop, which should reduce the damage they can deal back.

Checking type matchups: Garchomp is Dragon/Ground, so Dragon-type moves like Outrage hit it for super-effective damage (2x from the Dragon part, neutral from the Ground part), while Ground moves like Earthquake are neutral against it. Their Earthquake is likely what's been hurting our team so far.

Running the numbers, Outrage from our Garchomp with 182 Atk against their reduced Defense should deal roughly 258 damage with STAB and the type bonus, which looks like a clean KO on their ~157 HP Garchomp. Since we're also faster, Outrage is the clear choice here despite the confusion risk after multiple turns.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Incineroar is at 81/202 HP against Gholdengo at 90% health holding a Life Orb. Since Gholdengo is Steel/Ghost, Fire-type moves like Flare Blitz hit for double damage, making it a strong option despite the recoil.

Running the damage math, Flare Blitz with STAB and the Fire weakness looks like it should comfortably KO Gholdengo at its current HP, but speed matters — Gholdengo's base speed likely outpaces Incineroar, so it could strike first with Shadow Ball before I even get the chance to attack.

Fake Out won't work since Gholdengo is Steel/Ghost, immune to Normal moves. Gholdengo will likely outspeed and Shadow Ball first, so Protect just delays the inevitable, and Parting Shot fails outright since Good as Gold blocks status moves entirely.

Checking speed tiers confirms Gholdengo outpaces Incineroar, so I'm estimating whether its Shadow Ball with Life Orb and high Special Attack would be enough to knock out Incineroar outright.

It easily would, so Flare Blitz is risky unless I protect first. Protecting lets me scout this turn while Incineroar still faces the same speed and power disadvantage next turn, so I'll go with Protect.
